reasoning_traces.think:
The framework integrates three distinct yet interrelated probabilistic modules: scoring intensity via Poisson processes, set-length determination via logistic regression, and match outcome via another logistic model conditioned on set status. These components form a coherent Bayesian network where each module informs others—scoring drives set probability, which in turn influences win probability. The hierarchical structure allows for borrowing strength across teams, improving estimation stability. Team efficiency covariates (attack/defense) are embedded within the Poisson formulation, linking individual performance metrics to aggregate outcomes. This modular design supports uncertainty propagation across dependent variables, such as predicting both margin and win probability simultaneously. The use of scaled inverse-Wishart priors enables flexible covariance structures among team-level parameters, enhancing generalizability. The model assumes conditional independence within modules but acknowledges dependencies across them, providing a principled way to reason about complex sports dynamics.
